articleTitle: Autoencoder for 3D Palm Print Identification
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Information Technology, Applied Mathematics and Statistics (ICITAMS)
abstract: The issue of personal identification is growing due to how crucial it is to get over the constraints of the existing methods. The current methods have numerous drawbacks, such as the possibility of password forgetfulness and broken or stolen access cards. The significance of bioinformatics-related identification systems resulted from this. This study devised a new approach for recognizing people from images of their palmprints. The scanning equipment uses contactless 3D imaging to collect the input images. The proposed approach is based on Autoencoder. And the obtained results are promising. With 8 minutes of training, the model gave 98% accuracy for the testing dataset. The results are compared with the accuracy and training time of transfer learning-based models.

articleTitle: Air Pollution Prediction Using Machine Learning and Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Information Technology, Applied Mathematics and Statistics (ICITAMS)
abstract: With increased industrialization and urbanization, air pollution poses an environmental threat. Today, air quality is crucial for society and the environment. Due to increased air pollution, which has become a significant problem globally, accurate air pollution forecasting and prediction have become challenging and essential jobs. There are various numerical and statistical tools for predicting and analyzing the state of the air. However, for air quality prediction, the artificial neural network (ANN) is an effective data processing tool with high classification accuracy, a strong capacity for parallel processing, and a robust data learning ability to store data in a disturb Further more. As a result, this paper focuses on a survey review of recent air quality prediction techniques. Furthermore, it highlights the essentials.

articleTitle: Optimized GFDM Transceiver System Based on GA and ANN
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Information Technology, Applied Mathematics and Statistics (ICITAMS)
abstract: Generalized frequency division multiplexing (GFDM) is a multiple access scheme promising for the 5G standard. It presents exciting features such as low out-of-band and low peak-to-average power ratio. This paper optimizes the GFDM transceiver system using a Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Artificial Neural Network (ANN). GA optimizes the pulse shaping filter, which gives a new coefficient based on optimization processes. The ANN presented as an enhancement estimation method compared with Least Square (LS), the data set used to train the ANN generated by the transmitted pilot, received pilot and channel response. This data was used to train the ANN and replace the LS part. The ANN by three methods to choose the best performance under the different values of neurons. The proposed system presents enhancement in BER by 0.011 at 20 dB and 30 dB.

articleTitle: Multi-label Classification Technique of Chest X-Rays Image Based Cardiomegaly Disease Prediction
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Information Technology, Applied Mathematics and Statistics (ICITAMS)
abstract: One of the most common techniques used in detecting serious life-threatening diseases is chest X-Ray radiography, through which datasets of X-ray images are collected. Among the serious heart-related chest diseases that can be detected using this technique is Cardiomegaly. However, the X-ray image-based identification of diseases considers a time-consuming process and requires radiologists with high skills to interpret and analyze these images to accurately diagnose the pathologies, especially for difficult cases that cannot be interpreted by the naked eyes of humans where one image may have more than one pathology. In this context, to solve the above problems. in this paper, we deal with the above problems by designing the efficient architecture of two automated classification models based on the transfer learning technique and using the convolution neural network DenseNet121 as feature engineering. These architectures were constructed from DenseNet121 as a backbone model followed by a proposed deep neural network which consists of a global average pooling layer, two neural network layers, and an output layer. The first model was designed as a multi-label classification model to predict 8 types of chest diseases, thus the output layer contains 8 neurons and a sigmoid activation function, while the second model focused on the binary classification of cardiomyopathy so the output layer contains one neuron. Two custom functions were proposed for multi label classification model to be suitable for its task, loss function, and calculation of accuracy function. The performance of the models was implemented on the CheXpert dataset and evaluated in terms of accuracy and area under the curve (AUC). The results show that the first model achieved an AUC score of 90% and the second model obtained 83% which consider promising results. In addition, a web application interface was produced in this work which contributed to the practicality applicable to the model where it was examined in practical clinical to prove the generalization performance of the models, where the testing results were good and realistic.

articleTitle: A Developed Beyond 5G Massive Radio Access Networks Based On Artificial Intelligence Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Information Technology, Applied Mathematics and Statistics (ICITAMS)
abstract: The main aims of fifth-generation (5G) are to enhance the signal, improve quality of service (QOS) and make mobile service available everywhere for any device. It is also expected to open up new use cases for many vertical industrial applications, such as Healthcare, Education, public transportation, medical care, Autonomous Vehicles, public safety, Smart Cities, agriculture, manufacturing, and so on. The number of users, traffic, and data rate are expected to rise quickly. In the next infrequent years, mobile users and vertical industries will need new ways to meet their needs. Redesigning the network architecture, or rebuilding the radio access network, is a good choice among the available options. This study used Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) with an Adam optimizer algorithm to predict the best channel quality indicators (CQI). In this LSTM, weight vectors are made in a way that is based on each other. The Adam algorithm is used to find the best values for these weights. The experimental result considers how accurate the forecast was and how well the inventory was. The results of experiments show that Recurrent Neural Network (RNN-LSTM) with an Adam algorithm works well and makes fewer mistakes than other methods. We conclude that the proposed work with the Adam algorithm works well for predicting the quality indicators of the channel (CQI).

articleTitle: Deep Neural Network Based on A Stacked Autoencoder For 3D-Finger Knuckle Recognition
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Information Technology, Applied Mathematics and Statistics (ICITAMS)
abstract: The recognition of 3D_finger knuckle is unique to the encouraging biometric techniques, which has usual great interest recently due to its accuracy in recognizing individuals Though the literature observed several techniques and progresses to deal with the problem of identifying persons through the finger knuckle, the tools are still in its beginning. This paper offers an effective deep learning technique, stacked sparse autoencoders (SSAEs), to identify the individual through a 3d finger knuckle. The suggested method can extract features from finger knuckles and remove the exhausting use of features. Finally, a softmax classification model was introduced into stacked SAEs to classify a set of features. The suggested model was developed using three dimensions (3D) Finger Knuckle Images datasets from The Hong Kong Polytechnic University (PolyU);. The SSAE learns high-level features from just pixel intensities alone to identify distinguishing features of 3d finger knuckle images. Stacked autoencoders another better way for the feature extraction SSAE was shown to have an improved accuracy of 99%.

articleTitle: Engineering applications for Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in Embedded Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Information Technology, Applied Mathematics and Statistics (ICITAMS)
abstract: The fast-paced development of embedded systems and artificial intelligence (AI) in recent years has revolutionized the way we perceive the future. From industrial automation to human implants to exploring deep space, technologies such as artificial intelligence, machine learning, embedded systems (ES), internet of things (IoT) and their combinations are opening new doors to unexplored frontiers.

articleTitle: Stack of Heatmap Hourglass Network for Face Alignment
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Information Technology, Applied Mathematics and Statistics (ICITAMS)
abstract: This paper presents a new approach for facial landmark localization using a stack of hourglass models and an attention mechanism. The proposed method utilizes heatmap regression and a multi-stage architecture composed of hourglass networks to locate key points on a face, such as the eyes, eyebrows, nose, and mouth. The attention model focuses the network’s attention on specific features, enabling more accurate localization of facial landmarks. The model is trained on a largescale dataset using the Mean Squared Error loss function and evaluated on benchmark datasets. The results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance on three popular benchmark datasets, significantly improving the Normalized Mean Error metric (NME). The highest NME was 2.81 on the 300W data set. Fig. 1 shows some of our results. Furthermore, the method shows robustness to pose, illumination, and occlusion variations, making it a promising approach for real-world applications in face recognition, Face Age estimation, and facial expression analysis. The proposed method offers a promising solution for accurate and robust facial landmark localization in computer vision.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Minkowski Feature Selection for Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Information Technology, Applied Mathematics and Statistics (ICITAMS)
abstract: This paper proposes a design and implementation of a highly efficient feature selection based on Minkowski’s mathematical similarity for machine learning. Moreover, the development of the Minkowski feature selection can be general for intelligent datasets and machine learning. Intelligent optimizers and feature selection represent an advanced stage in machine learning and innovative computer applications by reducing the overall number of features to be included in the classification function process. This paper analyses Minkowski’s selection of best factors for EEG Bonn University data. Minkowski cancels the random movement and systematically limits the number of features and its point-to-point movement in order to promote exploration and reduce the probability of falling into stagnation. The main measures to analyze this research are Accuracy, precision, Recall, and F1score assessment. Moreover, the accuracy of Minkowski’s selection provided better classification results than some of the other approaches (100%)

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Smart Port Gate System Based on the Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Information Technology, Applied Mathematics and Statistics (ICITAMS)
abstract: Maritime transport is one of the cheapest types of transport, so international maritime trade has increased. Today, most countries with seaports are racing to transform their ports into smart ones to increase maritime trade and attract foreign investment. One of the most critical technologies in smart ports is the smart gate. It works on the speed of the flow of goods, which achieves higher returns and prevents manipulation and errors. This paper presents a smart gate that relies on several technologies, such as RFID, fingerprint sensors, and an automated license plate recognition system for authentication. In addition, computational clouds are used to store and process data. Where the results of these techniques are matched with the data stored in the cloud database, this work is considered an Internet of Things application. This gate has helped increase reliability and security and improve the appearance of the port and city. It also sends reports to the control centers that include all information about the movement of goods leaving the port to make all required statistics. The proposed smart gate port’s accuracy is up to 99.7%.

articleTitle: Blockchain Based Cloud Authentication Framework for Digital Identity Management in Smart City
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Information Technology, Applied Mathematics and Statistics (ICITAMS)
abstract: The smart city environment includes dozens or even hundreds of various services in various areas of interest to users and aimed at improving the standard of living. These include services related to very sensitive aspects such as health, education, banking, and services that have a secret aspect. Cloud service providers need user data in order to be able to authenticate him in order to be able to access and access the desired service. Therefore, confidentiality, privacy and security are essential conditions for this type of communication. This type of complex and intrusive services leads to the need to provide effective solutions and mechanisms for authentication processes based on digital identity information. The process of building and managing trust between service providers and users needs a system of standards, so this paper provides a framework based on the archived behavior of users and cloud service providers operating within the approved trust circle in a smart environment based on the blockchain and its advantages in reliability, transparency and decentralization, while providing a mathematical model for evaluating and calculating trust standards for all subscribers as a basis for completing the authentication process and accessing services.

articleTitle: Automatic Text Summarization-Based Transformers Architecture
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Information Technology, Applied Mathematics and Statistics (ICITAMS)
abstract: Summarization is the process of condensing a part of the text into a shorter version, decreasing the size of the original text while keeping the central informative and content significance. Because manual text summarizing is time-consuming and typically arduous, its automation is increasing in popularity, thus serving as a powerful stimulus for academic study. This work builds a model for an abstract text summarizer for the English language using the state-of-the-art “Transformer” model and self-attention mechanism on dataset SciTLDR of 5.4K. This dataset size cannot train the model in traditional deep learning methods such as RNN and LSTM. Also, it is challenging to train in machine learning as the number of samples is insufficient, and the model may suffer from under-fitting. The results of the Transformers model showed a good performance in the dataset size. The human evaluation results showed good performance in terms of Grammaticality, language cohesion, and non-repetition of information. This paper proposes an iterative data augmentation approach and an attention mechanism process in parallel; this is particularly helpful for datasets suffering from low resource conditions to get a better result.

articleTitle: Rabinovitch Hyper Chaotic Scrambling Based on Changing Pixels Values for Image Encryption
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Information Technology, Applied Mathematics and Statistics (ICITAMS)
abstract: In recent years, digital image is an important personal data that must be preserved from breaches and espionage. Because of the frequent circulation of images and their transmission through the Internet and social networking, many researchers wrote about encrypting images using chaos. In this paper, an algorithm is proposed to generate random locations based on the Rabinovitch Hyper Chaotic Systems (RHCS), which is used to encrypt images in all available cases of the value of pixels Changing: such as Row-Row Scrambling, Column-Column Scrambling, Row-Column Scrambling, bits in each Pixel Scrambling. The simulation results proved that merging methods (row, column, and row-column) and without merge scrambling give good results regarding encryption strength and time process. Moreover, the key space is very big, in all methods is 2585, and in row column, approach 21170

articleTitle: Dynamic Machine Learning Algorithms for Multiple Malware Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Information Technology, Applied Mathematics and Statistics (ICITAMS)
abstract: Vast volumes of data are readily available everywhere today. As a result, it is crucial to evaluate this data to draw out some relevant information and create algorithms based on that analysis. Algorithms are developed using machine learning (ML), which considers past connections and data trends. ML is utilized in various industries, including marketing, virus detection, and information retrieval. Using different machine learning methods, including Feed-Forward Neural Network (FFNN) and Support Vector Machine (SVM), this proposed system offers an analysis method for classifying malware into families. The proposal is a weight-based dynamic selection classification system. The study uses the DDoS 2019 dataset and the Microsoft Malware Classification Competition (BIG 2015) publicly accessible Kaggle database. The FFNN approach has a success percentage of 99.99%, but the SVM technology only manages 99.52%, according to the DDoS 2019 dataset. The Big 2015 dataset reveals that the FFNN had a success rate of 96.89%, whereas the SVM only showed an accuracy of 93.20 %.

articleTitle: ImageNet Classification using ResNet50 and Binary Marine Predators Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Information Technology, Applied Mathematics and Statistics (ICITAMS)
abstract: Image classification accuracy relies heavily on the quality of features used to classify the dataset. Researchers commonly use metaheuristic algorithms like the Marine Predators Algorithm (MPA) for feature selection and dimensionality reduction to enhance the accuracy and reduce the number of features required. In this study, we used a ResNet-50 convolutional neural network (CNN) pre-trained on ImageNet to extract features from the image dataset. We then utilized the Binary Marine Predator Algorithm (BMPA) to filter out irrelevant features and select the most pertinent ones from the feature vector extracted from the “avg_pool” layer in ResNet-50. Our proposed efficient approach can achieve superior classification accuracy and optimal feature selection. We anticipate that the combination of CNN and BMPA can be utilized in various other image classification tasks to enhance their performance.

articleTitle: A New Implementation of SHA-3 Hash Function Using Seed Value
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Information Technology, Applied Mathematics and Statistics (ICITAMS)
abstract: This paper aimed to suggest a new Secured Hash Algorithm 3 (SHA-3) with seed value implementation. Seed worth ensuring that there are fewer expectations collisions, despite an attacker selecting the data. Furthermore, attackers who combine seed values with hash functions are prevented from exploiting the properties of a hash function to construct many security attacks, such as denial of service attacks and dictionary attacks. A novel approach to enhanced SHA-3 diffusion was proposed here by XORing the seed value with $\theta$ step result after transforming the seed bits into a $5 \times 5 \times 64$ matrix and discarding the rest.

articleTitle: Lung Cancer Detection using Evolutionary Machine learning and Deep learning: A survey
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Information Technology, Applied Mathematics and Statistics (ICITAMS)
abstract: Lung Cancer is one of the world’s peak-level types of cancer. There are so many people are died due to lung cancer diseases. Early identification of tumors would facilitate in sparing a vast number of lives globally consistently. Computed tomography (CT) is essential for pulmonary nodule detection in diagnosing lung cancer. Recently, for creating medical image classification problems, machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) have emerged as two of the most popular and commonly utilized approaches. Furthermore, employing chest CT scans from pneumonia patients, ML and DL models outperformed conventional approaches in effectiveness. The structure and parameters of ML and DL models can be optimized using evolutionary algorithms (EA). This survey aims to overview the recent works in lung cancer detection-based ML and DL models that EA has optimized.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Localization Algorithm of RSS and TOA Based on Adaptive Weight Errors
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Information Technology, Applied Mathematics and Statistics (ICITAMS)
abstract: Specifying the location of wireless sensor devices is vital in many applications such as target tracking, remote environmental monitoring, and more. Time of arrival (TOA), the received signal strength indicator (RSSI) and range information are applied to locate the wireless sensor network (WSN) node’s location. Still, they suffer inaccuracy because of environmental factors in the 2D region. A ranging method has been suggested, merging the TOA information domain with RSSI to accurately determine the distance between the unknown node and the anchor node. This approach relies on utilizing RSSI and TOA ranging techniques in the near and far endings. We combine received signal strength indication and arrival time in parallel style as major elements. The findings of the two methods are then combined with the error percentage to determine the final location using adaptive weight errors. The proposed range method is promoted in this work to enhance the accuracy of the positioning. The proposal has been implemented by MATLAB simulation and the results show improving positioning accuracy compared to the conventional TOA and RSSI ranging method. The mean square error in the proposed method is 0.5044, whereas it was 0.7032 and 0.8102 in RSSI, respectively. This indicates that the suggested approach is more efficient and performs better for localization than the other two methods.

articleTitle: Review of Abnormalities Detection in IoT Using Evolutionary Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Information Technology, Applied Mathematics and Statistics (ICITAMS)
abstract: Today, the Internet is used for various applications such as sending or receiving emails, access to multimedia services, social networks, etc. Moreover, the population of people who use the Internet is increasing. Therefore, the issue of Internet of Things (IoT) security has become a major problem today. Recently, Deep Learning has become one of the most influential and valuable methods for detecting abnormalities in IoT Networks. Further, Deep Learning models produced more effective performance than traditional techniques in abnormalities detection. Moreover, the structure and parameters of ML and DL models can be optimized using evolutionary algorithms (EA). The survey aims to overview recent research on anomaly detection in the IoT-based Deep Learning model that EA has enhanced.

articleTitle: Enhancing Classification Performance through Efficient Feature Selection with SD-BMPA Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Information Technology, Applied Mathematics and Statistics (ICITAMS)
abstract: Feature selection is a critical step in the classification process that can improve accuracy by reducing the number of features in the data set. However, too many features can negatively impact accuracy, making selecting the most relevant ones challenging. In this study, a two-stage method for feature selection is proposed, which uses the Statistical Dependency (SD) and Binary Marine Predator Algorithm (BMPA) to identify and select the most significant features in the data set. The first stage involves identifying the most significant features in the data set using Statistical Dependency (SD). In the second stage, the Binary Marine Predator Algorithm (BMPA) is used to select a particular number of features that improve the classification accuracy established in the primary stage. The SD-BMPA algorithm is highly efficient and effective, resulting in improved classification accuracy compared to other methods. Furthermore, by converting continuous data into a discrete form and using metaheuristic algorithms, the SD-BMPA algorithm can handle large-scale data sets, making it suitable for various applications.

articleTitle: Survey on ML Investment in UAV Based Cellular Network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Information Technology, Applied Mathematics and Statistics (ICITAMS)
abstract: Positioning techniques of the mobile phone are one of the most important current and future trends because of their importance to human lives and their influential role in managing their affairs. For several reasons, unmanned aerial vehicle (UAVs) has recently been relied upon and used in cellular networks. First, providing network coverage in disaster-affected areas. Second, investing it in service based on demand. Finally, relying on the cellular network for UAV control and navigation instead of a Global Positioning System GPS-based navigation, due to the inability of the latter to work with specific cases, etc.). This new approach has resulted in new problems such as (coverage, connectivity, position location, and act) that must be to studied and solutions need to be found. Researchers made several attempts to solve these problems using traditional methods, but unfortunately, the results were unsatisfactory. Therefore, the other direction was to use and employ ML to solve these problems. This survey aims to highlight the use of ML in a UAV-based cellular network. Moreover, how to employ AI/ML in each method. In addition to identifying the most promising approach for the UAV to reach the desired results.

articleTitle: Hybrid Color Image Compression Using Signals Decomposition with Lossy and Lossless Coding Schemes
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Information Technology, Applied Mathematics and Statistics (ICITAMS)
abstract: This paper proposes a new, improved compression technique to compress color images. Compression knows days have become more critical because of the increasing demand for internet use and the exchange of many images, videos, and audio. This technique converts an image to YUV. The signal decomposition divides the image into significant components (C1) and small components (C2) parts; big indicates the energetic Component, and the detail is the small Component. Each Component is passed through different processing steps. The most vibrant part is passed through sequences of lossless coding steps to preserve the quality of the main features. The included coding steps are Bit plane Coding followed by Quadtree Coding. Meanwhile, the detailed Component was passed through a series of lossy coding steps using a controlled wavelet-based error criterion and quantization. Also, delta pulse code modulation (Delta PCM) was used to encode the (LL) component of the image due to its significance and to avoid causing significant distortions. While the rest components (LH, HL, HH) by discarding the small Bit plane and only encode the most important planes, the output of each encoded Bit plane is handled using Quadtree Coding. As a last stage of the energetic and detailed components, an adaptive shift coding. The proposed technique was tested on Lena and Baboon Images; testing results indicated that the suggested system could produce a good compression ratio while preserving the image's quality under control

articleTitle: A Survey on Iris Recognition Systems in Cross-Spectral Domain
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Information Technology, Applied Mathematics and Statistics (ICITAMS)
abstract: This paper provides a review of the biometrics system of the iris that has drawn far-reaching attention in recent years and applied in various fields such as applications in e-business and e-governance infrastructure and security fields, also a survey of the most recent research that deponed on iris recognition as considered to be the most reliable due to its high accuracy and unique the patterns in eye iris, large challenges when matching Iris images obtained through several domains (sensor/illumination) because different illumination factors result in the near-infrared (NIR) or visible light (VIS) spectral difference between the iris images recorded in single bands, where this causes performance degradation for iris recognition, what research performing during the last few decades that discuss several deep learning and machine learning techniques that have been applied to the creation of iris-based recognition systems. This paper presents a timeline, a technical overview, and a survey of various iris recognition techniques available in the literature to increase iris recognition’s precision in recent years.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Cloud Computing System to Manage the Working and Operation of Generators
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Information Technology, Applied Mathematics and Statistics (ICITAMS)
abstract: Control the operation of electric motors, track their performance, and ensure their load-bearing capacity. Essential to the maintenance of electric motors is monitoring their operating parameters. Monitoring the device’s temperature demonstrates that maximum heat makes the motor system unstable and shortens the equipment’s lifespan. Control and monitoring of electric motor operation and shutdown are designed to manage the obtained information by storing and retrieving it via a cloud computing system. Furthermore, at the facility where the engine is installed, an employee controls the operation and shutdown of the devices, including the site control process that includes the authority to oversee the management of the engine’s work or to control the management of the engine’s work remotely. In this respect, the supervisor has access to the on-off report of the management process. Overall, these advantages support the view that the suggested technique also aims to regulate the temperature of the engines by incorporating central air circulation when the temperature exceeds a particular threshold to maintain the temperature within a safe level. Central air conditioning is represented by fan operation, which disconnects it locally based on readings from temperature sensors. Display real-time information on a graphical user interface (GUI) for the supervisor and authorized personnel so they can make critical decisions regarding the electric motor. These reports are transmitted using online communication. Moreover, presenting it to the higher authorities in charge of designing the system’s front-end and back-end interfaces. These tasks can be done utilizing a home network site, flowing templates, hyperlinked syntax (PHP, CSS, HTML), and server hosting space (A2 Hosting). Likewise, this operating system has analyzed the current tasks of engine temperature and has argued that using the XAMPP software, a graphical user interface (GUI) is created to display data written in PHP and C-Sharp.

articleTitle: Behavior Analysis of Machine Learning Algorithms for Botnets Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Information Technology, Applied Mathematics and Statistics (ICITAMS)
abstract: Botnets constitute a significant cybersecurity threat becoming increasingly sophisticated and challenging to detect. In addition, they are used for various illegal activities, such as spreading viruses, conducting DDoS attacks, click fraud, phishing, and identity theft. This study focuses on the latest advancements in machine learning-based botnet detection research. It initially describes how ML technology is implemented in network security research and describes the properties regarding the botnet’s structure prior to the introduction of ML for botnet detection. Next, the study analyzes and summarizes the most commonly used ML algorithms and their security features in botnet detection. Finally, it concludes by summarizing the current ML solutions for describing, detecting, and researching botnets, as well as discussing how to evaluate the accuracy of botnet detection techniques.

articleTitle: Sentiment Analysis Using Word Sense Disambiguation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Information Technology, Applied Mathematics and Statistics (ICITAMS)
abstract: Sentiment analysis is crucial for many tasks and applications. For example, it is developed into a helpful tool for predicting market trends, monitoring social media, and being a reliable predictor of elections and products. For this task, numerous strategies were employed by researchers, ranging from rules-based strategies to machine learning and deep learning approaches to various data types. However, due to their failure to grasp the texts correctly, all of these techniques suffer from a lack of accuracy. In this work, an approach for extracting and using the (word sense disambiguation) of the word within the context is used as part of Initializing data and representing it. Two well-known algorithms were used (Bidirectional Long-Short Term Memory and Convolutional neural networks) for testing this approach in English. The system was evaluated using recall, precision, f-measure, and accuracy on the dataset (Amazon Kindle Store category). The results showed that the word sense disambiguation of the words is very useful, and the accuracy was increased by 4.21% for best cases and increased by 2% in worst cases. This work’s contribution can be summarized using word sense disambiguation (WSD), which aims to make the semantics of a word in context explicit by identifying the most appropriate meaning from a predefined sense, leading to many improvements in the performance of sentiment analysis.

articleTitle: Survey on Human Gender Classification Using Biometric Information
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Information Technology, Applied Mathematics and Statistics (ICITAMS)
abstract: One of the greatest vital and significant areas of research is the classification of gender. Gender classification is necessary and crucial for numerous commercial applications, including human-computer communication and computer-aided physiological or psychological analysis, because it comprises a varied range of information about the differences between male and female characteristics. To comprehensively assess gender classification research, this paper presents a survey of the available soft techniques for gender identification from biometric techniques, including biological information-based methods (biometric and bio-signal), and Non-Biological based methods (static and dynamic features). Iris recognition systems have drawn much interest among authentication methods because of their rich iris texture, which provides reliable standards for identifying people. However, most iris biometrics expertise and research have focused on identifying specific people. Therefore, this research can be seen as the first step in a more extensive investigation into iris recognition.

articleTitle: Alzheimer’s Disease Diagnosis using Deep Neural Network: Review
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Information Technology, Applied Mathematics and Statistics (ICITAMS)
abstract: Alzheimer’s disease is a neurological condition that is both chronic and irreversible, and there is currently no effective therapy for it. The symptoms are very modest initially, but they progressively worsen with time. If the patient and his family get an early diagnosis, they will have the chance to make choices about the future, which may include preparing for long-term care and legal and financial matters. Therefore, being able to accurately predict the progression of Alzheimer’s disease is essential for both clinical treatment and medical research. The diagnosis of Alzheimer’s disease is becoming ever more accurate as more aspects of healthcare are digitized. Several further strategies using machine learning have been proposed. Now, in the present day, deep learning has shown promising results in diagnosing Alzheimer’s disease. Various deep networks exist, such as the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), which has 2D and 3D capabilities. Therefore, the authors of this publication would be interested in researching other works in this sector that may be used in conjunction with magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to identify this illness. These works, together with their comparisons and discussions, will be presented.

articleTitle: Development of a Control System for Autonomous Mobile Robots: a Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Information Technology, Applied Mathematics and Statistics (ICITAMS)
abstract: Autonomous Mobile Robots (AMRs) are currently employed in various fields, including manufacturing, warehousing, hospitals, and terminals, thanks to their advanced hardware and control software, which allows them to operate independently in complex environments. In contrast to an Automatic Guided Vehicle (AGV), where the unit manages the routing, planning, and dispatching for all AMRs, AGVs can negotiate and communicate independently with multiple sources, leading to decentralized decision-making for vehicles and buildings. These unique features have spurred traditional decision-making techniques to incorporate and adapt to AMRs. This review identifies and categorizes studies related to AMR planning and management in intralogistics, focusing on the impact of technological advancements on planning and choice management. We aim to enhance the literature by including AMR development plans and modifying manual managers’ decision-making models to achieve better outcomes.

articleTitle: Violence Scene Detection from Social Media Networks Using Artificial Intelligence Methods
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Information Technology, Applied Mathematics and Statistics (ICITAMS)
abstract: Social media networks. Despite all of the benefits and positive aspects of social media, it is essential to remember that these platforms are not often a secure environment for communication, exchanging ideas and information, and creating online communities. Social media violence can be divided into three categories: cyberbullying, comments, and violent events such as protests and homicides. Furthermore, social media posts include textual as well as visual content. This work seeks to catalyze academics who want to tackle the study of Violence Detection (VD) and get knowledge of the key problems that need to be resolved in this rapidly developing area, where vd is a specific issue within the more prominent topic of action recognition. The goal of violence detection is to identify whether or not violence happens in a short amount of time automatically and efficiently. There is a wide range of algorithms used to detect violence, including Convolution Neural Networks (CNN), You Only Look Once (YOLO), Support Vector Machines (SVM), etc., which will be presented in this research.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation Of Cloud Computing System for Station Networks 400KV
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Information Technology, Applied Mathematics and Statistics (ICITAMS)
abstract: The benefits of computing to systems that can be integrated with computers due to their multitasking ability are being improved by distributed and cloud computing developments. This is already the case (SG) when talking about the Smart Grid. Previously, the data of the 400kV network was sent to the National Control Center through a remote terminal unit (RTU), and the process of storing information is limited. In the event of an expansion of the 400kV network, this requires replacing a complete system and a small storage capacity. This improvement can boost energy management system efficiency in the production, transmission, and distribution of power. Since electricity has essentially replaced all other forms of energy on the planet, it is only natural that every country, even emerging ones like Iraq, seeks to constantly improve its ability to produce electrical energy by integrating network and computing infrastructure. The use of cloud computing technology for smart grid management is discussed in this article, including parameters of the grid on the cloud system, and seeks to lower investment costs of data storage devices for the power sector to enable operation may push parameters or update the data of the grid on the cloud system in a flexible and highly secure manner. The use of cloud computing to store and transmit data from 400kV.networks in the Middle Euphrates power-producing plants to the National Control Center is also covered in this article.

articleTitle: Machine Learning for Detection and Classification of Human Brain Tumor: A Survey
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Information Technology, Applied Mathematics and Statistics (ICITAMS)
abstract: Intracranial solid tumors arise due to uncontrolled and abnormal cell division. Classification of brain tumors depends on factors such as the tumor’s location, the type of tissue it consists of, its malignant or benign nature, and other factors. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is one of the techniques frequently used to detect tumors in the brain Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). It provides important detail that is used in accurately scanning the human body’s internal organization. problem with brain tumors is the complexity and variations in tumor location, shape, size, and intensity from patient to patient. Also, tumor boundaries are usually unclear and irregular. Some studies have appeared in the detection and classification of human brain tumors. Therefore, some of these studies will be discussed in this paper. Humans have developed many algorithms to get better results in brain tumor detection. They used the latest machine-learning techniques to solve this problem. Through these studies, we conclude that the best accuracy was achieved using deep learning techniques like Deep Auto-Encoder (DAE) based on Jaya Optimization Algorithm (JOA) for classification and Bayesian Fuzzy clustering (BFC) to segment up to 98.5%.

articleTitle: Blockchain Based Digital Identity Management System for Smart City Services
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Information Technology, Applied Mathematics and Statistics (ICITAMS)
abstract: Centralized systems that require third parties remain opaque and represent a single point of failure. Therefore, in accordance with the requirements of cloud services and identity management mechanisms, it is necessary to move towards more transparent and collaborative methods. That is, all service providers under the same federation deal positively with the issued identity of the user. The distributed format gives good potential for ID management systems and treats everyone with the same level of validity. This paper presents a blockchain-based identity management system for the purpose of creating a federated identity management system that is used by multiple organizations by Taking advantage of decentralization and high transparency in the blockchain. Several vital advantages of blockchain are positive for forming identity management systems characterized by transparency and high security, and privacy. Implementing the proposed system on a private Hyperledger Fabric blockchain network proved effective according to the criteria studied, and there is also great potential for improvement. The practical application of the proposed system proved high quality and promising possibilities in blockchain based identity management.

articleTitle: Unsupervised Automated Keyphrase Extraction Approaches: A Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Information Technology, Applied Mathematics and Statistics (ICITAMS)
abstract: Because of technical improvements and the exponential growth of textual data and digital sources, extracting high-quality keywords at a high level in research is now more challenging. Keyphrase extraction characteristics, which are growing in popularity, are required for high-level keyword extraction. Automated keyphrase extraction (AKE) aims to find the significant subjects of a text document by automatically identifying a small group of single or multi-words from inside the text. AKE is crucial to many NLP and information retrieval tasks, including document summarizing and classification, article recommendation, and full-text indexing. This paper presents a survey of various techniques available for keyphrase extraction, discusses some important feature selection methods utilized by researchers to rank candidate keyphrases based on their importance, and finally debates various benefits and drawbacks for each category.

articleTitle: A Review of Emotions Recognition via Facial Expressions for Human-Robot Interaction
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Information Technology, Applied Mathematics and Statistics (ICITAMS)
abstract: One of the most intriguing challenges in human-robot interaction is whether it can reinforce robots with emotional intelligence to make the interaction more intuitive, realistic, and natural. Emotion recognition is widely researched in broader areas such as human-computer interaction and affective computing. Here we report on recent advances in emotion recognition, particularly in the case of human-computer interaction. Our goal is to analyze the current situation regarding accepted emotion paradigms, interaction styles, and classification strategies, as well as provide insights to focus on facial expressions and how the form of emotions are classified, then provide a list of available datasets containing data for these modalities and the challenge faced by facial expression procedures. Moreover, show a Summarization of Details about the commonly used “Recognition mode, Recognized emotions, Robot Type, Sensor, Algorithm, Methodology, Dataset, Performance metrics, and Results.” This review describes recent research on emotional facial expressions during human-robot interactions. Offers different perspectives for future research.

articleTitle: Survey Convolution Neural Network based on Blockchain Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Information Technology, Applied Mathematics and Statistics (ICITAMS)
abstract: Deep learning and blockchain technology are key techniques for smart applications. Because it can make wise judgments, deep learning has become quite popular in the last few years. With blockchain technology development, connecting it with deep learning techniques like the convolutional network is feasible to benefit from its unique properties. One of the most crucial characteristics of blockchain technology that may be used for convolutional networks is the provision of trust, transparency, security, authentication, reliance on decentralized servers, independence from third parties, and no single point of failure. As a result, we investigate the significance of combining blockchain technology with deep learning applications in this study. We examine recent research that focuses on combining deep learning applications with blockchain technology. By doing this, we provide meaningful debates on two topics: To provide decentralized security and data integrity in the Blockchain using deep learning techniques. The specifics of the data sets were also addressed by outlining their benefits and drawbacks.
